rule: section 2.8 (forum and dispute-forum allocations owe no counterparty performance -- v0.68, REVIEWER-RULED, this segment is the motivating case); with sections 3.2.1 and 8.8/3.5 disposing of the other three sentences, leaving ZERO obligation-bearing clauses and so failing section 2's 1-3 band as well
reason:
Submission-to-jurisdiction / waiver-of-venue boilerplate. FOUR sentences, offsets verified by execution via corpus.split_sentences(), and NOT ONE is obligation-bearing.

S1 [0:48] '(a) Submission to Jurisdiction; Waiver of Venue.' -- a heading, no modal, no clause.

S2 [49:510] THE ONLY LIVE CANDIDATE, and the segment's reason for existing in the record: 'Each Party hereto agrees that any action, proceeding or claim it commences against the other Party pursuant to this Agreement shall be brought [page artifact] in the courts of the United States for the Southern District of New York...'. EXCLUDED under section 2.8 on the ground that a forum allocation OWES NO COUNTERPARTY PERFORMANCE -- it fixes the legal position of a dispute that may never arise rather than requiring either party to render anything to the other in the course of performing the agreement. No deliverable, no deadline, no correlative party owed a performance; a party that never commences an action can never fail to comply.

TWO NEARER-LOOKING GROUNDS WERE CONSIDERED AND BOTH SET ASIDE AS NON-DECIDING, recorded here so a future reader does not reconstruct the ruling from the wrong one.
(a) NOT the thing-subject ground. S2's operative subject is 'any action, proceeding or claim', a non-party, which is what C10-029 and C04-163 were excluded on -- but that ground is UNAVAILABLE here: C04-03 and C14-05 are LOCKED ITEMS whose spans are thing-subject agentless passives, so a non-party grammatical subject has never been sufficient to exclude.
(b) NOT the taxonomy gap. Under the competing reading the performance is 'bringing an action in a named court' and NO member of ACTIONS denotes it (COMPLY, read that way, would swallow any duty whatever and collapse the taxonomy). That observation is REAL and DOES NOT DECIDE: section 8.8 exists so a genuine taxonomy gap is annotated with the nearest verb and TAGGED rather than excluded, and section 3.7 requires known-gap forms to be annotated normally rather than avoided. Had this clause owed a counterparty performance the absent verb would have made it an action_not_in_taxonomy ITEM, not an exclusion.
(c) NOT section 2.5 either, which is the trap this ruling is written to avoid. Section 2.5's PRINCIPLE ('a future state worth monitoring') fits comfortably, but its OPERATIVE TRIGGER is unreviewable discretion (section 2.5.1's 'in its sole business judgment'), which a forum clause has none of -- and section 8.8.4 already corrected a disposition that stretched section 2.5 across exactly this distance. Hence a new section rather than a citation.

THE COUNTER-READING, recorded rather than defeated. S2 carries 'shall', its operative verb 'be brought' is a performance rather than a copula, and a filing in the wrong court is observable -- so it can fairly be read as a conditional duty (if you sue, sue here) whose breach a court itself remedies by dismissal or transfer. On that reading the item would carry obligor: ABSENT and obligee: ABSENT under section 3.5.3 ('Each Party' is the subject of 'agrees', 'it' the agent of 'commences'; neither occupies a core argument slot of 'shall be brought'), making it the SECOND both-ABSENT item after C14-06. What decides against it is that the constraint runs to the FORUM rather than to the counterparty.

S3 [511:1127] 'Each Party HEREBY irrevocably and unconditionally submits to the jurisdiction ... and irrevocably and unconditionally WAIVES ...' -- section 3.2.1's present-tense self-executing performative class, whose own rule text names 'hereby waives' in terms. Takes full effect at execution, so no future state remains to monitor.

S4 [1128:1387] 'Each Party agrees that a final non-appealable judgment ... shall be conclusive and binding and may be enforced in other jurisdictions ...' -- subject is 'a final non-appealable judgment', a thing; 'shall be conclusive and binding' is COPULAR STATUS (section 8.8) and 'may be enforced' a right on that same non-party subject. Same class as C10-029 (severability, no party subject anywhere) and C04-163.

COST, MEASURED RATHER THAN ASSERTED, and it is why this ruling is about the record and not about a number: FIGURE-NEUTRAL on every published figure -- in-force criterion 2 5/10 = 50.0%, all-items 7/15 = 46.7%, K 14/32, A 7/27, 60 items over 35 segments, all unchanged and confirmed by a real run_scoring.run() AFTER the ruling (15 items scored, 45 cassette-unscoreable, teardown clean) rather than hand-computed. NEITHER DISPOSITION COULD HAVE MOVED THE HEADLINE FIGURE, so the ruling could not have been reached for to protect one.

reason:
'Section 4.4 Effect of Termination' -- effect-of-termination / survival boilerplate. TWO sentences, offsets verified by execution via corpus.split_sentences(), and NEITHER CLAUSE COMMANDS OR PERMITS PARTY CONDUCT, which is the ground of exclusion.

S1 [0:34] 'Section 4.4 Effect of Termination.' -- a heading, no modal, no clause.

S2 [35:672] carries two verb phrases and both state a legal effect rather than a duty:
  (a) '...this IP Agreement and the rights and obligations of the parties under this IP Agreement, including any obligation to make any assignment or grant any license hereunder, AUTOMATICALLY END without any liability against any party or its Affiliates' -- a PRESENT-INDICATIVE LEGAL EFFECT WITH NO MODAL AT ALL. Nothing is commanded; the clause states what happens to the agreement upon an event. Nearest precedent C04-163 clause (1), 'The termination of this Agreement ... shall not operate to relieve Bellicum from its obligation to pay' -- a savings/interpretive clause about a pre-existing obligation. If anything this is weaker than C04-163's, which at least carries a 'shall'.
  (b) '...the provisions of this Section 4.4, Article V, Section 6.1, ... and Section 6.13 WILL REMAIN IN FORCE AND SURVIVE any termination of this IP Agreement' -- section 3.2's 'will'-FUTURE-FACT pattern. Section 3.2's rule is explicit: 'will' is MUST when it states a party's undertaking and 'is not an obligation at all when it states a future fact about the agreement'. A survival clause states a future fact about which provisions of the document keep operating -- not an undertaking by anyone. DIRECT PRECEDENT, SAME DOCUMENT: C22-045 clause (3), 'the provisions of this IP Agreement will control', excluded in batch 3 as 'section 3.2's future-fact pattern (a future fact about how the documents relate, not a party's undertaking), not a MUST'. The subject noun phrase is the same shape -- 'the provisions of ...' -- and the pattern is identical.

THE THING-SUBJECT POINT IS CORROBORATION ONLY, NOT THE GROUND -- the same discipline applied at C04-172 in this batch, and stated here so a future reader does not reconstruct the ruling from it. Both subjects are indeed non-party ('this IP Agreement and the rights and obligations of the parties'; 'the provisions of this Section 4.4, Article V, ...'), and C22-045's own rule line leads with that point. But a non-party grammatical subject CANNOT carry an exclusion on its own: C04-03 and C14-05 are LOCKED ITEMS whose spans are thing-subject agentless passives ('Each quantity of Miltenyi Product(s) ... shall be delivered'). What excludes this segment is that neither clause commands or permits conduct by anyone -- one is an automatic legal effect, the other a future fact about the document. The thing-subject observation corroborates that reading and does not establish it.

VERIFIED BY EXECUTION RATHER THAN READ OFF THE PROSE, and re-verified at write time: the segment contains EXACTLY ONE MODAL in 672 characters -- 'will' at offset 602, governing '... and Section 6.13 will remain in force and survive' -- and NO PARTY OCCUPIES A SUBJECT SLOT ANYWHERE. The only three party mentions are 'the parties' at 150 (a possessive inside 'the rights and obligations of the parties'), 'party' at 319 and 'Affiliates' at 332 (both objects of the preposition in 'without any liability against any party or its Affiliates').

ZERO obligation-bearing clauses, so section 2's '1-3 obligation-bearing clauses' band is failed from below and the segment is excluded WHOLE.

rule: section 2 (exceeds the 1-3 obligation-bearing clause band -- FOUR clauses); the third and fourth are S4's two clauses, split on OBLIGOR under section 4.3
reason:
'2.8. COMPONENT END OF LIFE.' -- a component end-of-life provision. FOUR sentences, FOUR obligation-bearing clauses, so section 2's '1-3 obligation-bearing clauses' band is EXCEEDED and the segment is excluded WHOLE on the MECHANICAL ground -- the same disposition as C04-029, C14-139, C14-028, C17-077, E03-013, E03-018 and C02-049, and under C14-139's own process rule: ELIGIBILITY IS DECIDED BEFORE CONTENT IS ADJUDICATED, and the live judgment calls are preserved as forward guidance in this entry rather than cashed in on this segment.

THE COUNT WAS VERIFIED BY EXECUTION, NOT EYEBALLED. The segment carries FIVE modal occurrences; exactly ONE of them lives inside the definitional parenthetical, leaving FOUR operative:
  (1) S2 [28:233] 'Contractor SHALL take all necessary measures in order to receive immediate updates from its suppliers regarding end of life of any component' -- obligor Contractor.
  (2) S3 [234:338] 'Contractor SHALL notify NICE immediately upon becoming aware of the event of end of life of a component' -- obligor Contractor.
  (3) S4a [339:507] 'In such event, NICE SHALL designate and approve the replacement components to be used instead' -- obligor NICE.
  (4) S4b [339:507] 'and the Parties WILL mutually agree on the required changes in APPENDIX C' -- obligor the Parties. `will` + a party subject stating an undertaking is MUST under section 3.2, and C04-07 is the locked precedent for exactly 'the Parties will ... agree'.

S4a AND S4b SPLIT ON OBLIGOR UNDER SECTION 4.3, which is what makes the count 4 rather than 3. The two clauses have DIFFERENT OBLIGORS -- NICE designates and approves; the Parties agree the resulting APPENDIX C changes -- and one item holds ONE obligor slot, so they cannot be one item however section 4.3 is read. Independently breachable: NICE can designate without the Parties ever agreeing the APPENDIX C changes, and the agreement obligation can fail with the designation already made. Same arithmetic as C04-017's S2 earlier in this batch, which yielded C04-14 and C04-15 for the same reason.

THE PARENTHETICAL IS NOT COUNTED, and its modal is the fifth occurrence: '(i.e types of components which SHALL no longer be manufactured)'. It is DEFINITIONAL -- it says what 'end of life' MEANS -- and its subject is 'types of components', a THING rather than a party, so it imposes no duty on anyone. Excluded on section 3.5's non-party-subject ground and on section 2's definitions row, either sufficient. Its offset was asserted at write time and the modal inside it identified by position rather than by reading, so the 5-minus-1 arithmetic is checked rather than claimed. S1 [0:27] is a heading.

THE EXCLUSION HOLDS UNDER BOTH READINGS OF THE ONE UNADJUDICATED CALL, which is why that call does not need deciding here -- see the forward-guidance observation below. Whether S4a's 'designate and approve' is ONE compound action (section 8.3 branch 1, one item tagged `compound_action`) or TWO separate performances (section 4.3, two items) changes the count from FOUR to FIVE. Both exceed the 1-3 band, so the segment is excluded either way and the question is genuinely moot FOR ELIGIBILITY. Stated explicitly rather than left implicit, because C14-139's process rule exists precisely to stop an eligibility decision from resting on a content call that was never made.

GUARDS RUN FIRST AND BOTH CLEAN, re-verified at write time. F27 (splitter over-split): ZERO redaction markers and ZERO abbreviation dots, so all four of `split_sentences()`'s fragments are real and no rejoin is needed -- note 'i.e' appears WITHOUT a trailing period ('i.e types'), which is why the splitter correctly did not break there; had it carried one, this would have been an F27 case. Section 8.7 (page furniture): NONE. Measured document-agnostically by RECURRENCE rather than by a literal string -- no 6-or-8-word run from this segment recurs in 5 or more of C14's 153 pool segments -- with C04's own header gated as a known answer first. That detector was REBUILT at C03-125 in this same batch after the string-keyed version returned a FALSE NEGATIVE on a segment that was ~50% furniture.

COST: FIGURE-NEUTRAL. No item is added, so in-force criterion 2 stays 5/10 = 50.0% and all-items 7/15 = 46.7%; the set stays at 64 items over 38 segments.
observations: FORWARD GUIDANCE, DELIBERATELY NOT ADJUDICATED, per C14-139's process rule: IS 'designate and approve' ONE COMPOUND ACTION OR TWO? Section 8.3's branch determinant would have to run -- do `designate` and `approve` map to DIFFERENT taxonomy verbs (branch 1, tag compound_action) or the SAME one (branch 2, no tag)? APPOINT is the plausible mapping for `designate`; `approve` has no obvious taxonomy member, which would pull toward branch 3 (compound_action AND action_not_in_taxonomy). Section 4.3's prior question is whether they are aspects of ONE indivisible performance (designating a replacement component IS approving it, in a single act of selection) or two separate performances (a party could designate a component and withhold approval). NOT DECIDED HERE, and the exclusion does not depend on it -- see the both-readings paragraph in the reason field.

A SECOND LIVE CALL, also preserved rather than cashed in: S3's temporal 'immediately upon becoming aware of the event of end of life of a component' trips TWO known gaps at once -- 'immediately' is a vague qualifier (section 15.2) and 'upon <trigger>' is a preposition `_RELATIVE_RE` rejects (section 8.9's relative_trigger_preposition). Which governs, and whether section 8.6's one-tag rule applies to this pair the way it applied at C04-16 to redacted_value-versus-within_preposition, is a real question this segment would have forced. It is recorded because the next annotator to draw an 'immediately upon' temporal will face it, and NO queue row is opened: the pairing question is the same shape section 8.6's rule already governs, so it is not a new question until a segment makes it one.

NO QUEUE ROW IS OPENED BY THIS EXCLUSION, which is a deliberate statement rather than an omission. Both live calls above are applications of existing rules -- section 8.3's branch determinant and section 8.6's one-tag rule -- to a segment that is excluded before either is reached. Nothing here is a NEW question, and C14-139's precedent is that forward guidance lives in the exclusion entry rather than becoming a row.

rule: section 2 (no obligation-bearing clause -- NO PARTY CONDUCT IS COMMANDED); the four modal clauses are FORM requirements and DEEMING provisions by kind; thing-subject and self-containment are CORROBORATION ONLY
reason:
'12.5 Notices.' -- a notices provision. TWO sentences, FOUR modal clauses, and NOT ONE OF THEM COMMANDS OR PERMITS PARTY CONDUCT, which is the ground of exclusion. Zero obligation-bearing clauses, so section 2's 1-3 band is failed FROM BELOW.

THE FOUR CLAUSES BY KIND, each a FORM requirement or a DEEMING provision rather than a duty. Offsets asserted at write time:
  (1) [61] 'All notices and other communications hereunder SHALL BE IN WRITING' -- a FORM requirement on the notice itself. It prescribes what a notice must look like to count, not what any party must do.
  (2) [85] '...and SHALL BE DEEMED GIVEN if delivered personally or by electronic mail or facsimile transmission (receipt verified), telexed, mailed by registered or certified mail ...' -- an express DEEMING provision. 'shall be deemed' states a legal consequence that follows automatically from a state of affairs; nobody is directed to do anything.
  (3) [411] '(or at such other address for a Party as SHALL BE SPECIFIED by like notice' -- passive, and its subject is 'such other address', a thing.
  (4) [492] 'provided, that notices of a change of address SHALL BE EFFECTIVE only upon receipt thereof)' -- a status/effectiveness statement whose subject is 'notices of a change of address'.

THE THING-SUBJECT POINT IS CORROBORATION ONLY, NOT THE GROUND -- the same discipline applied at C04-172 and C22-039 earlier in this batch. A non-party grammatical subject cannot carry an exclusion by itself, because C04-03 and C14-05 are LOCKED ITEMS whose spans are thing-subject agentless passives. What excludes this segment is that every clause states the FORM a notice must take or the EFFECT it has, and none directs a party to act. The subjects corroborate that reading.

VERIFIED BY OFFSET RATHER THAN BY READING, and re-asserted at write time: the four 'shall' occurrences sit at 61, 85, 411 and 492, and the segment's ONLY two 'Party' tokens sit at 335 and 402, BOTH as OBJECTS OF PREPOSITIONS -- 'to the Parties at the following addresses' (governed by 'to') and 'for a Party as shall be specified' (governed by 'for'). An object of a preposition cannot be the subject of a modal, which is what makes the 'no party conduct' finding mechanical rather than interpretive.

SELF-CONTAINMENT IS A SECOND, INDEPENDENT GROUND AND IS ALSO CORROBORATION ONLY: the segment ENDS ON A COLON, introducing an address list that lies entirely OUTSIDE it (asserted at write time). That fails section 2's 'is self-contained' test, checked per sentence under section 2.6. It is not the ground because with no obligation-bearing clause there is no scored field for the missing addresses to be depended on -- section 2's cross-reference row is never reached.

COST: FIGURE-NEUTRAL. No item is added, so in-force criterion 2 stays 5/10 = 50.0% and all-items 7/15 = 46.7%; the set stays at 64 items over 38 segments.

Section 3.5's non-party-subject test is deliberate and is not in question; what the pair shows is that the IR's coverage of this requirement is a function of DRAFTING STYLE rather than of extraction quality. reason:
A DIP-payoff consequence clause, enumerated item (xlii) of a list. ONE sentence, ONE modal, and NO PARTY CONDUCT IS COMMANDED anywhere in it -- that is the PRIMARY ground.

THE OPERATIVE CLAUSE IS AN AUTOMATIC LEGAL EFFECT, NOT A DUTY: 'all ongoing commitments under the DIP Credit Agreement (as defined in the Final DIP Order) SHALL BE CANCELED AND TERMINATED'. It states what HAPPENS to the commitments once the DIP Payoff is received -- a consequence that follows automatically from a state of affairs -- rather than directing any party to do anything. reason:
Item (i) of a two-item warranty list. ONE sentence, two modals, both `will`, both with `Material` as subject.

THE LEAD GROUND IS THE MISSING STEM, AND IT WAS FOUND BY READING THE NEIGHBOUR RATHER THAN THIS SEGMENT. C03-130 ENDS with the warranting predicate: "For the duration of such warranty period, Vendor represents and warrants to AT&T as follows:" -- asserted at write time, including that C03-130 ends on that colon. So the verb that makes this a promise (`represents and warrants`), the obligor (`Vendor`) and the obligee (`AT&T`) ALL sit OUTSIDE this segment. Section 3.5 requires the party alias verbatim from inside the span and forbids importing a parent stem, so the span cannot supply obligor or obligee on ANY reading of the clause.

THIS IS EXPRESSLY NOT A RULING THAT WARRANTIES ARE NOT PROMISES. A warranty is a binding undertaking; what is absent here is not the promise but the span-internal means of annotating it. The same clause with its stem inside the span would be a different disposition, which is exactly what the queue row's forcing function asks for.

VERIFIED BY OFFSET, not by reading: the ONLY party token in the whole segment is `AT&T` at 24, inside the object-modifying parenthetical `(excluding AT&T Provided Equipment)` -- a modifier of the subject noun phrase, never the subject of a modal. `Vendor`, `Commnet`, `Party`/`Parties`, `warrants` and `represents` do not occur in the segment at all. The same by-offset check settled C02-079 and C06-028 earlier in this batch.

CORROBORATION ONLY, and labelled as such on this batch's own discipline: the subject `Material` is a THING (section 3.5) and the first predicate is copular -- `will be merchantable, free from defects ..., fit and sufficient ..., free from all Liens` (section 8.8's status class). NEITHER can carry an exclusion alone, because C04-03 and C14-05 are LOCKED items whose spans are thing-subject agentless passives. Nor does section 3.2's `will` row decide it on its own: `will` + a party subject stating an undertaking is MUST (C04-14 earlier in this batch), and the reason it is not MUST here is that there is no party subject, which is the lead ground again.

E03-03 IS DISTINGUISHED ON SPAN-INTERNAL AVAILABILITY, NOT ON WHETHER A GUARANTEE IS A DUTY. E03-03 is a LOCKED item -- "Each Party hereby guarantees the performance by its Affiliates of such Party's obligations" -> MUST / ENSURE / action_not_in_taxonomy, reviewer-ruled obligation-bearing against a section 3.2.1 exclusion. Its span CONTAINS the promissory verb AND its obligor. C03-131's contains neither. That is the whole distinction; nothing in E03-03's ruling is narrowed.

SET ASIDE AS NON-DECIDING, and said to be: WARRANT and GUARANTEE are both ABSENT from ACTIONS (execution-checked, as are CONFORM and PERFORM). Real, but section 8.8 exists so that a genuine taxonomy gap is annotated-and-TAGGED rather than excluded, and section 3.7 forbids avoiding known-gap forms -- so a missing verb could never be the ground. E03-03 is the proof: it is a taxonomy gap AND an item.
